{"decision":"Recorded as BRAINSTORMING, not as a proposal. Anthony, 2026-09-06, in his words: 'adding /topic or /topic-search skill — some times, I just want to see what's already within the reflow2 graph and it isn't a brainstorm or link-artifacts type effort — I just want to see something about a topic.' Distinct from dec:idea-should-the-open-list-be-rendered-in-the-owners-language-rather-than-the-graphs (qs): that renders the OPEN LIST in the owner's vocabulary; this renders the design's knowledge of ONE SUBJECT. Same family (a projection in the reader's words), different question.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, and why it is not this: search_design returns ranked hits — ids and names, one dimension; get_node reads one node; where-am-i reads back the WHOLE design's state; relation_candidates and surprising_connections work outward from one node. None answers 'what do we know about X' as a digest: what is decided about it and why, what is still open, what has been measured, what realizes or checks it, and what is conspicuously absent.

OPTIONS:
(a) A SERVED SKILL `topic`: given a phrase, the agent runs search_design (top N), groups hits by node type, pulls each hit's one-hop neighbourhood and status, and renders a bounded digest in the owner's vocabulary (the lens), with a line for what the search did NOT find. No writes. Cheapest to ship; costs 5-10 calls per topic and the rendering is the agent's, so two agents could render the same topic differently.
(b) A TOOL `topic_report(query)` computed server-side: same digest, deterministic, one call, reply-cost bounded by the server; a skill becomes a one-line instruction leg pointing at it. The SE doctrine on record — views are PURE PROJECTIONS of the graph and a renderer's fill-ins are defects — argues the projection belongs in the server, not in an agent's prose.
(c) EXTEND where-am-i with a `topic` argument, reusing its read-back voice. Cheap; but where-am-i is the whole-design orientation and its skill text is already long — mixing scopes makes both harder to read.
(d) NOTHING NEW: search_design + get_node already do it by hand. (a) also adds reply cost — fact:defect-the-reply-costs-more-than-the-answer is open — and a digest per topic that is not bounded becomes the verbose-reply problem in a new coat. (b) is the honest home by the projection doctrine and by cost (one call, server-bounded), but it is a new tool on a surface whose sibling-inconsistency is the largest open friction class — it must take the ONE naming convention Anthony just ruled (type optional, resolved from the id) from day one. (c) is free and wrong-scoped. (d) is what he has. A RANKING IS A FINDING, NOT A DECISION: (b) with a thin skill as its instruction leg, and the not-found line mandatory; (a) as the prototype that discovers what the digest should contain before the tool freezes it.
